why: All three checks pass, so the divergence stands. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks.md line 102 reads exactly 'A `loop.md` file replaces the built-in maintenance prompt with your own instructions.' The rest of that line narrows rather than reverses it ('It defines a single default prompt for bare /loop, not a list of separate scheduled tasks, and is ignored whenever you supply a prompt on the command line.'). The remaining claimed behaviour is on the same page: :108-:109 give the two scopes with '.claude/loop.md — Project-level. Takes precedence when both files exist.' over '~/.claude/loop.md'; :120 gives both re-read and truncation — 'Edits to loop.md take effect on the next iteration ... Keep the file concise: content beyond 25,000 bytes is truncated.' The only carve-out (:123) is Bedrock/AWS/Google/Foundry, which does not apply to us. (2) CITED LINE CONFIRMED: packages/shared/src/prompts/__tests__/system.test.ts:351-352 is inside `it('guards cycles while expanding @path imports')` and writes AGENTS.md containing '@loop.md' plus a loop.md containing '@AGENTS.md' — an arbitrary filename in an import-cycle fixture, nothing to do with scheduling. Exactly as claimed. (3) ONE LAYER UP / ONE LAYER DOWN, consequence verified separately from the identifier: `grep -rain 'loop\.md|loopMd|LOOP_MD'` over packages/*/src and apps/*/src returns only that fixture plus five comment citations of the unrelated page agent-sdk/agent-loop.md. `grep -rain 'ScheduleWakeup'` over src returns zero. No 'maintenance prompt' / defaultPromptFile constant exists. Bundled skills are only plugin-creator and skill-creator (apps/electron/resources/skills), so there is no /loop skill for a loop.md to default. No loop.md file exists anywhere in the tree. The sibling-subsystem trap does not apply: the neighbouring cron subsystem (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/cron-tools.ts, tool-defs.ts CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete) is fully built and carries an inline prompt per task — it reads no default-prompt file at any scope, so nothing upstream already handles this. NOT an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 lists nine 'do not fix' decisions (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — none of them is loop.md or /loop. NOT a rebrand/product difference either: the fork's own plan intended it under a renamed path and never built it. It IS a recorded open gap, not a hidden one — docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:201-204 costs loop.md as Task 3 of four in the unbuilt /loop unit ('project file first (<project>/.nessy-agent/loop.md, our .claude/loop.md), then user (<configDir>/loop.md), re-read every iteration, truncated past 25 000 bytes'), and the deviation register carries 'not implemented — requires /loop' at :297 and :514. An acknowledged, costed, unbuilt item is still a divergence, not a decision with a reason.
correctedState: Confirmed, with the scope corrected upward. There is no production reader for `loop.md` at either scope — the single grep hit (packages/shared/src/prompts/__tests__/system.test.ts:351-352) is an @path import-cycle fixture that merely reuses the filename. But `loop.md` is not a standalone gap: the entire `/loop` half of scheduled-tasks.md is absent — no bundled `/loop` skill (apps/electron/resources/skills holds only plugin-creator and skill-creator), no `ScheduleWakeup` tool (zero hits across packages/*/src and apps/*/src), no built-in maintenance prompt, and no self-paced mode. So a `loop.md` reader alone would have no bare-`/loop` entry point to default, which is why the fork's own plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:201-204) files it as Task 3 of a four-task unit gated on a missing bundled-command tier. The cron half IS at parity (CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete in packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts, closed as R27b). Two documentation artifacts understate this: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:208 marks `scheduled-tasks` green with 'R3 — all built', and the deviation register records only `ScheduleWakeup` ('not implemented — requires /loop', :297 and :514) without a row for `loop.md` or the maintenance prompt.
